annotation.kind: reconstruction of equation (8)'s linked inherited-right first-order error contribution

assumptions: The matrix dimension is positive and the exact and computed operands are real square n-by-n matrices, as in equation (1) and the recursive-inversion application of equation (8).
One otherwise unspecified matrix norm is used throughout and satisfies nonnegativity, definiteness, homogeneity, subadditivity, and submultiplicativity.

The computed product is linked to exact operands, inherited left and right perturbations, local multiplication error, and a higher-order remainder; the first-order error removes the inherited cross product and that remainder.
The actual right perturbation norm is bounded by the nonnegative absolute inherited error err(B,n).
Machine epsilon is positive and mu is nonnegative, although neither appears in the selected inherited-right term; no per-run global polynomial-growth premise is added.

The selected result uses the finite real-valued first-order regime; exceptional values, the inherited-error cross product, and the unspecified local higher-order remainder are outside this contribution.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p10_t1_inherited_right_product_error {n : Nat} (run : P10FirstOrderProductRun n) : P10InheritedRightEquation8Term run
formal_statement.plain_language: For a linked first-order product, the realized first-order error decomposes into the local, inherited-right A*dB, and inherited-left dA*B matrices, and the selected right matrix is bounded by ||A||*err(B,n).

informal_proof: Expand the linked computed-product equation and cancel the exact product, inherited perturbation cross product, and higher-order remainder to derive the three-matrix first-order decomposition. Then apply submultiplicativity to A*dB and multiply the supplied ||dB|| <= err(B,n) bound by the nonnegative norm ||A||.
informal_statement: Equation (8)'s inherited-right first-order contribution, linked through a derived three-source decomposition to the realized first-order product error and bounded with the source's coefficient and operand orientation.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The complete 24-module frozen baseline has no declaration deriving the exact three-source first-order matrix decomposition from this linked product execution or identifying its inherited-right component under an unspecified consistent norm. MatrixAlgebra contains generic finite-product and concrete Frobenius bounds, but neither preserves this source-specific execution and error decomposition.

source_locations.role: stable matrix-multiplication model and unspecified norm convention
linked first-order amplification of error inherited from the right operand and its additive position

tier_rationale: After the source execution is packaged in P10FirstOrderProductRun, the proof directly expands and cancels the linked product equation to expose the three first-order matrices, then specializes one submultiplicativity certificate and the supplied right-inherited-error bound. The frozen baseline has related generic and concrete product-norm results but no theorem preserving this linked decomposition and unspecified-norm component semantics.
